contentBlocks.body: NULL means "unknown" or "missing", not zero and not an empty string. Any comparison involving NULL (=, <>, <, >) produces a third truth value, UNKNOWN. SQL's logic therefore has three values: TRUE, FALSE, and UNKNOWN. WHERE, ON, and HAVING keep a row only when the predicate is TRUE, so UNKNOWN rows are dropped just like FALSE ones.

contentBlocks.code:
-- AND: FALSE wins, otherwise UNKNOWN wins over TRUE
TRUE  AND UNKNOWN  -- UNKNOWN
FALSE AND UNKNOWN  -- FALSE
-- OR: TRUE wins, otherwise UNKNOWN wins over FALSE
TRUE  OR  UNKNOWN  -- TRUE
FALSE OR  UNKNOWN  -- UNKNOWN
-- NOT flips TRUE/FALSE but leaves UNKNOWN alone
NOT UNKNOWN        -- UNKNOWN

NULL = NULL        -- UNKNOWN (use IS NULL instead)

contentBlocks.body: The classic trap is NOT IN with a NULL in the list. `x NOT IN (1, 2, NULL)` expands to `x <> 1 AND x <> 2 AND x <> NULL`. The last comparison is always UNKNOWN, so the whole predicate can never be TRUE, and the query returns zero rows. It happens silently whenever the subquery's column is nullable.

NOT IN and NOT EXISTS also differ for the outer row: an order with a NULL customer_id is dropped by NOT IN (NULL <> anything is UNKNOWN), but NOT EXISTS keeps it, because no blocked row can match NULL. Know which answer your feature needs.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Model `SELECT id FROM orders WHERE customer_id NOT IN (SELECT customer_id FROM blocked)` with real three-valued logic. `NOT IN` is TRUE only if every `<>` comparison is TRUE; any NULL on either side makes that comparison UNKNOWN. An empty blocked list makes NOT IN TRUE for every row. Return the ids of the rows kept, in input order.
What does `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM users WHERE manager_id = NULL` return when 12 users have no manager?

payload.explanation: manager_id = NULL is UNKNOWN for every row, so no row passes the filter. Write manager_id IS NULL.

choices: NULL is not allowed with OR
payload.explanation: OR is TRUE if either side is TRUE. Here neither side is known to be TRUE, and one side might be, so the result is UNKNOWN.

knowledgeItems.prompt: Name the subquery operator that is safe when the subquery column may contain NULLs.

payload.text: Replace `WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT ...)` with `WHERE NOT ____ (SELECT 1 FROM ... WHERE ...)` to avoid the NULL trap.
